verses.context: After warning against trusting powerful people who eventually die, this psalm calls truly happy the one whose hope rests instead in the God of Jacob.

KJV.text: The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.
KJV.displayText: The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.

BSB.text: The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion.
BSB.displayText: The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion.

CPDV.text: The Lord is well pleased with those who fear him and with those who hope in his mercy.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord is well pleased with those who fear him and with those who hope in his mercy.

verses.context: This psalm of praise notes that what pleases the Lord is not raw strength, like a fast horse, but people who fear him and hope in his mercy.

KJV.text: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
KJV.displayText: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

BSB.text: When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.
BSB.displayText: When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.

CPDV.text: When you slumber, you shall not fear. When you rest, your sleep also will be sweet.
CPDV.displayText: When you slumber, you shall not fear. When you rest, your sleep also will be sweet.

verses.context: Part of a longer promise that wisdom brings safety, Solomon pictures a person lying down at night without fear and sleeping soundly.

KJV.text: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness: but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.
KJV.displayText: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness: but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.

BSB.text: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.
BSB.displayText: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.

CPDV.text: The expectation of the just is rejoicing. But the hope of the impious will perish.
CPDV.displayText: The expectation of the just is rejoicing. But the hope of the impious will perish.

verses.context: Contrasting the outcomes awaiting the righteous and the wicked, Solomon promises hope brings gladness while wicked expectation comes to nothing.

KJV.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
KJV.displayText: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

BSB.text: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
BSB.displayText: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.

CPDV.text: The soul that blesses shall be made fat. And whoever inebriates will likewise be inebriated himself.
CPDV.displayText: The soul that blesses shall be made fat. And whoever inebriates will likewise be inebriated himself.

verses.context: Praising generosity, Solomon observes that the person who gives freely ends up enriched, and the one who refreshes others is refreshed in turn.

KJV.text: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.
KJV.displayText: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.

BSB.text: Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
BSB.displayText: Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.

CPDV.text: He who makes promises is also jabbed, as if with a sword, in conscience. But the tongue of the wise is reasonable.
CPDV.displayText: He who makes promises is also jabbed, as if with a sword, in conscience. But the tongue of the wise is reasonable.

verses.context: Contrasting careless and wise speech, Solomon compares reckless words to a sword's cutting wound, while the wise person's words bring healing.

KJV.text: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.
KJV.displayText: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.

BSB.text: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
BSB.displayText: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.

CPDV.text: The well-being of the heart is life for the flesh. But envy is decay for the bones.
CPDV.displayText: The well-being of the heart is life for the flesh. But envy is decay for the bones.

verses.context: Comparing inward states rather than outward circumstances, Solomon credits a peaceful heart with giving life to the body, while envy rots it from within.

KJV.text: A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.
KJV.displayText: A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.

BSB.text: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.
BSB.displayText: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.

CPDV.text: A rejoicing heart gladdens the face. But by the grief of the soul, the spirit is cast down.
CPDV.displayText: A rejoicing heart gladdens the face. But by the grief of the soul, the spirit is cast down.

verses.context: Turning to matters of the heart, Solomon observes that a cheerful heart shows on the face, while sorrow of heart breaks the spirit.

KJV.text: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the Lord, happy is he.
KJV.displayText: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the Lord, happy is he.

BSB.text: Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.
BSB.displayText: Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.

CPDV.text: The learned in word shall find good things. And whoever hopes in the Lord is blessed.
CPDV.displayText: The learned in word shall find good things. And whoever hopes in the Lord is blessed.

verses.context: Linking practical skill to spiritual trust, Solomon promises good outcomes to whoever handles matters wisely and happiness to the one who trusts the Lord.

KJV.text: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.
KJV.displayText: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.

BSB.text: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.
BSB.displayText: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.

CPDV.text: Whoever conceals an offense seeks friendships. Whoever repeats the words of another separates allies.
CPDV.displayText: Whoever conceals an offense seeks friendships. Whoever repeats the words of another separates allies.

verses.context: On handling another's fault, Solomon praises the one who covers an offense out of love, over the one who gossips and divides close friends.

KJV.text: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
KJV.displayText: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.

BSB.text: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.
BSB.displayText: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.

CPDV.text: The doctrine of a man is known through patience. And his glory is to pass beyond iniquities.
CPDV.displayText: The doctrine of a man is known through patience. And his glory is to pass beyond iniquities.

verses.context: Praising self-control over quick offense, Solomon credits wisdom with delaying anger, treating overlooking an insult as honorable rather than weak.

KJV.text: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee.
KJV.displayText: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee.

BSB.text: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
BSB.displayText: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.

CPDV.text: Do not say, “I will repay evil.” Wait for the Lord, and he will free you.
CPDV.displayText: Do not say, “I will repay evil.” Wait for the Lord, and he will free you.

verses.context: Countering the urge toward personal revenge, Solomon instructs the wronged person to wait on the Lord for deliverance instead of repaying evil directly.

KJV.text: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the Lord.
KJV.displayText: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the Lord.

BSB.text: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.
BSB.displayText: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.

CPDV.text: The horse is prepared for the day of battle. But the Lord bestows salvation.
CPDV.displayText: The horse is prepared for the day of battle. But the Lord bestows salvation.

verses.context: Closing a chapter weighing human planning against God's sovereignty, Solomon notes a war-horse can be readied, but victory ultimately belongs to the Lord.

KJV.text: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.
KJV.displayText: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.

BSB.text: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!
BSB.displayText: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!

CPDV.text: If you despair, being weary in the day of anguish, your strength will be diminished.
CPDV.displayText: If you despair, being weary in the day of anguish, your strength will be diminished.

verses.context: Speaking plainly about crisis, Solomon observes that a person's true strength, or the lack of it, shows most clearly on a hard day.

KJV.text: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
KJV.displayText: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.

BSB.text: Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off.
BSB.displayText: Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off.

CPDV.text: So, too, is the doctrine of wisdom to your soul. When you have found it, you will have hope in the end, and your hope shall not perish.
CPDV.displayText: So, too, is the doctrine of wisdom to your soul. When you have found it, you will have hope in the end, and your hope shall not perish.

verses.context: Comparing wisdom to honey a son is urged to taste, Solomon promises that finding it brings a real future reward rather than disappointment.

KJV.text: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.
KJV.displayText: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.

BSB.text: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
BSB.displayText: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.

CPDV.text: Whoever fears man will quickly fall. Whoever hopes in the Lord shall be lifted up.
CPDV.displayText: Whoever fears man will quickly fall. Whoever hopes in the Lord shall be lifted up.

verses.context: Contrasting two sources of security, Solomon warns that fearing what people think becomes a trap, while trusting the Lord keeps a person safe.

KJV.text: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
KJV.displayText: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.

BSB.text: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
BSB.displayText: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.

CPDV.text: Who shall find a strong woman? Far away, and from the furthest parts, is her price.
CPDV.displayText: Who shall find a strong woman? Far away, and from the furthest parts, is her price.

verses.context: Opening the closing poem of Proverbs, this verse poses a question about the rare value of a capable, virtuous woman, worth more than costly jewels.

KJV.text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.
KJV.displayText: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.

BSB.text: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
BSB.displayText: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!

CPDV.text: If one falls, he shall be supported by the other. Woe to one who is alone. For when he falls, he has no one to lift him up.
CPDV.displayText: If one falls, he shall be supported by the other. Woe to one who is alone. For when he falls, he has no one to lift him up.

verses.context: Reflecting on the value of companionship over isolation, the Preacher observes that a person who falls alone has no one there to help them up.

KJV.text: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
KJV.displayText: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.

BSB.text: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
BSB.displayText: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.

CPDV.text: In the same manner that you do not know the way of the spirit, nor the way that bones are joined together in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you do not know the works of God, who is the Maker of all.
CPDV.displayText: In the same manner that you do not know the way of the spirit, nor the way that bones are joined together in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you do not know the works of God, who is the Maker of all.

verses.context: Comparing the mystery of the wind and of a child forming in the womb, the Preacher argues that God's ways are simply beyond full human understanding.

KJV.text: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.
KJV.displayText: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.

BSB.text: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
BSB.displayText: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.

CPDV.text: Chorus to Groom and Bride: Capture for us the little foxes, which are tearing down the vines; for our vineyard has flourished. Bride to Chorus: My beloved is for me, and I am for him. He pastures among the lilies, until the day rises and the shadows decline. Bride to Groom: Return, O my beloved. Be like a doe and like a young stag upon the mountains of Bether.
CPDV.displayText: Chorus to Groom and Bride: Capture for us the little foxes, which are tearing down the vines; for our vineyard has flourished. Bride to Chorus: My beloved is for me, and I am for him. He pastures among the lilies, until the day rises and the shadows decline. Bride to Groom: Return, O my beloved. Be like a doe and like a young stag upon the mountains of Bether.

verses.context: In this love poem, the young woman describes her beloved as belonging entirely to her, picturing him among the lilies of the field.

KJV.text: And it shall be said in that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the Lord; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation.
KJV.displayText: And it shall be said in that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the Lord; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation.

BSB.text: And in that day it will be said, “Surely this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He has saved us. This is the LORD for whom we have waited. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”
BSB.displayText: And in that day it will be said, “Surely this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He has saved us. This is the LORD for whom we have waited. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”

CPDV.text: And they will say in that day: “Behold, this is our God! We have waited for him, and he will save us. This is the Lord! We have endured for him. We will exult and rejoice in his salvation.”
CPDV.displayText: And they will say in that day: “Behold, this is our God! We have waited for him, and he will save us. This is the Lord! We have endured for him. We will exult and rejoice in his salvation.”

verses.context: Looking ahead to a day when death itself is swallowed up, Isaiah pictures God's people finally saying that the Lord they waited for has brought salvation.

KJV.text: For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.
KJV.displayText: For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.

BSB.text: For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand and tells you: Do not fear, I will help you.
BSB.displayText: For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand and tells you: Do not fear, I will help you.

CPDV.text: For I am the Lord your God. I take you by your hand, and I say to you: Do not be afraid. I have helped you.
CPDV.displayText: For I am the Lord your God. I take you by your hand, and I say to you: Do not be afraid. I have helped you.

verses.context: Reassuring an anxious Israel, God through Isaiah promises to hold their right hand personally and tells them plainly not to be afraid.

KJV.text: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.
KJV.displayText: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.

BSB.text: Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray. I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you.
BSB.displayText: Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray. I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you.

CPDV.text: Even to your old age, I am the same. And even with your grey hairs, I will carry you. I have made you, and I will sustain you. I will carry you, and I will save you.
CPDV.displayText: Even to your old age, I am the same. And even with your grey hairs, I will carry you. I have made you, and I will sustain you. I will carry you, and I will save you.

verses.context: Contrasting himself with idols that must be carried by their worshippers, God tells Israel through Isaiah that he is the one who carries his people, even into old age.

KJV.text: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.
KJV.displayText: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.

BSB.text: For thus says the One who is high and lifted up, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the oppressed and humble in spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the contrite.
BSB.displayText: For thus says the One who is high and lifted up, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the oppressed and humble in spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the contrite.

CPDV.text: For this is said by the Most High, the Sublime One, who dwells in eternity. And his name is Holy, for he dwells in the exalted and holy place, and he acts with a restrained and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
CPDV.displayText: For this is said by the Most High, the Sublime One, who dwells in eternity. And his name is Holy, for he dwells in the exalted and holy place, and he acts with a restrained and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.

verses.context: Describing God as both transcendent and near, Isaiah says the eternal, holy God chooses to dwell with those who are humble and repentant in heart.

KJV.text: And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.
KJV.displayText: And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.

BSB.text: The LORD will always guide you; He will satisfy you in a sun-scorched land and strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.
BSB.displayText: The LORD will always guide you; He will satisfy you in a sun-scorched land and strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.

CPDV.text: And the Lord will give you rest continually, and he will fill your soul with splendor, and he will free your bones, and you will be like a watered garden and like a fountain of water whose waters will not fail.
CPDV.displayText: And the Lord will give you rest continually, and he will fill your soul with splendor, and he will free your bones, and you will be like a watered garden and like a fountain of water whose waters will not fail.

verses.context: Explaining what true fasting looks like, Isaiah promises that caring for the hungry and afflicted will bring the Lord's continual guidance and refreshment.

KJV.text: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.
KJV.displayText: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.

BSB.text: For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.
BSB.displayText: For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.

CPDV.text: For behold, I create the new heavens and the new earth. And the former things will not be in memory and will not enter into the heart.
CPDV.displayText: For behold, I create the new heavens and the new earth. And the former things will not be in memory and will not enter into the heart.

verses.context: Looking far beyond present judgment, God announces through Isaiah a coming new creation so complete that the old troubles will not even be remembered.

KJV.text: Thy words were found, and I did eat them; and thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart: for I am called by thy name, O Lord God of hosts.
KJV.displayText: Thy words were found, and I did eat them; and thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart: for I am called by thy name, O Lord God of hosts.

BSB.text: Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words became my joy and my heart’s delight. For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts.
BSB.displayText: Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words became my joy and my heart’s delight. For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts.

CPDV.text: I discovered your words and I consumed them. And your word became to me as the gladness and joy of my heart. For your name has been invoked over me, O Lord, the God of hosts.
CPDV.displayText: I discovered your words and I consumed them. And your word became to me as the gladness and joy of my heart. For your name has been invoked over me, O Lord, the God of hosts.

verses.context: Despite his hard calling, Jeremiah tells God that receiving God's words brought him real joy, since he was known as one who carried God's name.

KJV.text: But the Lord is with me as a mighty terrible one: therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and they shall not prevail: they shall be greatly ashamed; for they shall not prosper: their everlasting confusion shall never be forgotten.
KJV.displayText: But the Lord is with me as a mighty terrible one: therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and they shall not prevail: they shall be greatly ashamed; for they shall not prosper: their everlasting confusion shall never be forgotten.

BSB.text: But the LORD is with me like a fearsome warrior. Therefore, my persecutors will stumble and will not prevail. Since they have not succeeded, they will be utterly put to shame, with an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.
BSB.displayText: But the LORD is with me like a fearsome warrior. Therefore, my persecutors will stumble and will not prevail. Since they have not succeeded, they will be utterly put to shame, with an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.

CPDV.text: But the Lord is with me, like a strong warrior. For this reason, those who persecute me will fall, and they will be ineffective. They will be greatly confounded. For they have not understood the everlasting disgrace that will never be wiped away.
CPDV.displayText: But the Lord is with me, like a strong warrior. For this reason, those who persecute me will fall, and they will be ineffective. They will be greatly confounded. For they have not understood the everlasting disgrace that will never be wiped away.

verses.context: Even while lamenting the mockery and plots against him, Jeremiah declares confidence that the Lord stands with him like a fearsome warrior, so his enemies will fail.

KJV.text: Ah Lord God! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:
KJV.displayText: Ah Lord God! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:

BSB.displayText: “Oh, Lord GOD! You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too difficult for You!

CPDV.displayText: Alas, alas, alas, O Lord God! Behold, you have made heaven and earth, by your great strength and by your outstretched arm. No word is difficult for you.

verses.context: After buying a field as a sign of future hope even while Jerusalem is besieged, Jeremiah prays, marveling that nothing is too difficult for the God who made heaven and earth.

KJV.displayText: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.

BSB.displayText: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king.

CPDV.displayText: For behold our God, whom we worship, is able to rescue us from the oven of burning fire and to free us from your hands, O king.

verses.context: Facing execution in a furnace for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego declare their confidence that God can deliver them.

KJV.text: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
KJV.displayText: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

BSB.displayText: But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.”

CPDV.text: But even if he will not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not worship your gods, nor adore the gold statue, which you have raised up.”
CPDV.displayText: But even if he will not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not worship your gods, nor adore the gold statue, which you have raised up.”

verses.context: Immediately after affirming God's power to save them, the three men add that even if he chooses not to, they will still refuse to worship the king's image.

BSB.text: Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is,’ or ‘There it is.’ For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”
BSB.displayText: Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is,’ or ‘There it is.’ For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”

CPDV.text: And so, they will not say, ‘Behold, it is here,’ or ‘Behold, it is there.’ For behold, the kingdom of God is within you.”
CPDV.displayText: And so, they will not say, ‘Behold, it is here,’ or ‘Behold, it is there.’ For behold, the kingdom of God is within you.”

verses.context: Answering Pharisees who ask when God's kingdom will arrive, Jesus tells them it will not come as a visible spectacle, since it is already present among them.

KJV.text: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
KJV.displayText: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.

BSB.text: But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
BSB.displayText: But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”

CPDV.text: But I have prayed for you, so that your faith may not fail, and so that you, once converted, may confirm your brothers.”
CPDV.displayText: But I have prayed for you, so that your faith may not fail, and so that you, once converted, may confirm your brothers.”

verses.context: Warning Peter that Satan wants to test him, Jesus says he has already prayed for Peter's faith to hold, so that Peter can later strengthen the other disciples.

KJV.text: And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?
KJV.displayText: And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

BSB.text: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
BSB.displayText: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”

CPDV.text: And they said to one another, “Was not our heart burning within us, while he was speaking on the way, and when he opened the Scriptures to us?”
CPDV.displayText: And they said to one another, “Was not our heart burning within us, while he was speaking on the way, and when he opened the Scriptures to us?”

verses.context: After the risen but unrecognized Jesus explains the scriptures to two travelers on the road to Emmaus, they later recall how their hearts burned within them as he spoke.

KJV.text: And of his fulness have all we received, and grace for grace.
KJV.displayText: And of his fulness have all we received, and grace for grace.

BSB.text: From His fullness we have all received grace upon grace.
BSB.displayText: From His fullness we have all received grace upon grace.

CPDV.text: And from his fullness, we all have received, even grace for grace.
CPDV.displayText: And from his fullness, we all have received, even grace for grace.

verses.context: Reflecting on Jesus as the Word made flesh, John describes believers as continually receiving grace upon grace out of his abundant fullness.

KJV.text: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
KJV.displayText: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.

BSB.text: But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.”
BSB.displayText: But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.”

CPDV.text: Instead, the water that I will give to him will become in him a fountain of water, springing up into eternal life.”
CPDV.displayText: Instead, the water that I will give to him will become in him a fountain of water, springing up into eternal life.”

verses.context: Talking with a Samaritan woman at a well, Jesus contrasts ordinary water with the water he offers, which permanently satisfies and leads to eternal life.

KJV.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.
KJV.displayText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.

BSB.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.
BSB.displayText: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.

CPDV.text: Amen, amen, I say to you, that whoever hears my word, and believes in him who sent me, has eternal life, and he does not go into judgment, but instead he crosses from death into life.
CPDV.displayText: Amen, amen, I say to you, that whoever hears my word, and believes in him who sent me, has eternal life, and he does not go into judgment, but instead he crosses from death into life.

verses.context: Speaking about the authority given to him by the Father, Jesus promises that whoever hears his word and believes has already crossed from death into life.

KJV.text: He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.
KJV.displayText: He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.

BSB.text: Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: ‘Streams of living water will flow from within him.’”
BSB.displayText: Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: ‘Streams of living water will flow from within him.’”

CPDV.text: whoever believes in me, just as Scripture says, ‘From his chest shall flow rivers of living water.’”
CPDV.displayText: whoever believes in me, just as Scripture says, ‘From his chest shall flow rivers of living water.’”

verses.context: Standing up during the Feast of Tabernacles, Jesus cries out that whoever believes in him will have rivers of living water flowing from within them.

KJV.text: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.
KJV.displayText: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.

BSB.text: So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
BSB.displayText: So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.

CPDV.text: Therefore, if the Son has set you free, then you will truly be free.
CPDV.displayText: Therefore, if the Son has set you free, then you will truly be free.

verses.context: Speaking to Jews who claim never to have been enslaved, Jesus tells them that real freedom, the kind he offers, is the only freedom that lasts.

KJV.text: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.
KJV.displayText: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.

BSB.text: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.
BSB.displayText: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.

CPDV.text: And I give them eternal life, and they shall not perish, for eternity. And no one shall seize them from my hand.
CPDV.displayText: And I give them eternal life, and they shall not perish, for eternity. And no one shall seize them from my hand.

verses.context: Describing himself as the good shepherd, Jesus promises his sheep eternal life so secure that no one can snatch them out of his hand.
